hardware.summary: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz, 8 logical cores, 8.4 GB RAM, Windows

rows.name: Analysis per reading, one channel (median / p95)
rows.includes: Parsing the 4-channel ASCII file, validation, band-pass, Hilbert envelope, FFT, defect-band features. Warm, single process, 200 runs.

rows.name: Signal processing only (median)
rows.includes: Validation and features for one channel, excluding file parsing.

rows.name: HTTP /api/analyze round trip (median / p95)
rows.includes: Local upload of a 0.55 MB file, parsing, analysis and JSON response. Server limited to 1 BLAS thread. 35 warm runs.

rows.name: Server cold start
rows.includes: Python interpreter start, imports and first /api/health response.

rows.name: Server memory (resident)
rows.includes: Whole process tree (on Windows this includes the small venv launcher). Measured after serving the largest replay (Test 3), a spectrum, and 40 live analyses.

rows.name: Single logical core (CPU affinity pinned): analysis per reading (median / p95)
rows.includes: Same work as the first row, in a separate process pinned to one core, 200 runs. Peak memory of that process: 109 MB. No memory cap was enforced.

rows.name: Learned state per bearing
rows.includes: A median and a spread for each of three defect families. There is no trained model file.

rows.name: Precomputed replay artifacts
rows.includes: All replays and stored spectra for the demo. Not needed for live analysis.

note: Measured on a developer laptop. The single-core row pins the process to one logical core; it is not a 0.5-CPU / 256 MB container, which was not run because Docker was unavailable on the build machine. Server-side timings on the deployed Railway service are in results/deploy-verification.json.
